Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. The Namibian openers, Jan Frylinck and Louren Steenkamp, are out in the middle and it will be Gurjapneet Singh will be bowling the first over for India A.
... The Run Chase ...

A massive mountain for Namibia - The stage is now set for a fascinating second half as Namibia prepares to hunt down this mammoth target. While the scoreboard pressure is immense, the Namibian side will be backing themselves to play fearlessly and navigate the Indian bowling attack. On a surface that has played well for the batters so far, a strong start in the Powerplay will be essential for the Associate nation to stay in the hunt. All eyes now turn to the chase to see if Namibia can pull off a stunning result or if the India A bowlers will defend their total with clinical precision.

Namibian bowlers fight back against batting might - The bowling effort from Namibia was tested against a batting-heavy Indian lineup, and while they conceded a significant total, there were notable individual contributions. Max Heingo, Ruben Trumpelmann, and Gerhard Erasmus were the pick of the bowlers, each picking up two wickets to break crucial partnerships. Bernard Scholtz and Willem Myburgh also chipped in with a wicket apiece, showing resilience in the middle overs. Despite the massive target looming over them, the Namibian unit stuck to their task well, ensuring the chase remained within the realm of possibility if their top order fires.

Parag and Ashutosh power India A to a formidable total - After winning the toss and opting to bat first, India A justified their decision by posting 197 on the board that sets a steep challenge for the Namibian side. The innings was anchored by a standout performance from Riyan Parag, who emerged as India's best batter with a commanding 69. His ability to clear the fence at will and rotating strike kept the scoreboard ticking, providing the backbone for the Indian effort. The momentum was further boosted in the latter stages by Ashutosh Sharma, who provided a flourishing finish with a handy knock in the 30s, ensuring India A finished with a total that would take some serious chasing.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set. The players are out in the middle. Priyansh Arya and Urvil Patel to open for India A. Ruben Trumpelmann to bowl first.

Namibia's skipper - Gerhard Erasmus says they would have bowled first as they batted first in the previous game. Shares that they haven't played on this ground but it looks like a high scoring pitch. Hopes to keep India under 180. Mentions that they want some stability before going to the big event. Acknowledge that they are coming after playing some good cricket recently, all in all, they have gained a lot of momentum.

India's captain - Ayush Badoni says they will bat first as the wicket looks flat and his batters could score freely. Reckons that they haven't set a total but they are looking for a score above 200. Informs that Tilak Varma is out and Ashutosh Sharma replaces him.

Namibia - Alexander Volschenk, Dylan Leicher, Louren Steenkamp, Malan Kruger, Gerhard Erasmus (C), JJ Smit, Jan Frylinck, Jan Nicol Loftie-Eaton, Zane Green (WK), Ben Shikongo, Bernard Scholtz, Jack Brassell, Jan Balt, Max Heingo, Ruben Trumpelmann and Willem Myburgh.

India A - Shreyas Iyer, Ashutosh Sharma, Ayush Badoni (C), Priyansh Arya, Tilak Varma, Naman Dhir, Riyan Parag, Vipraj Nigam, Narayan Jagadeesan, Urvil Patel (WK), Ashok Sharma, Gurjapneet Singh, Khaleel Ahmed, Manav Suthar, Mayank Yadav and Ravi Bishnoi.
TOSS - Up goes the coin, and it lands in favour of Ayush Badoni. India elect to BAT first!

Moulding the bench strength - For India A, the focus is on individual fitness and bench strength. All eyes are on Narayan Jagadeesan, who struck a brilliant century in the previous warm-up game. Also, pace sensation Mayank Yadav and all-rounder Riyan Parag are seeking to demonstrate full match fitness after their respective rehab stints at the CoE. The India A squad shows the depth that the nation possess. Can the home team win the final Warm-up game before the mega event kicks off? Stay tuned to find out. Toss and team sheets next.

A force to reckon with - For Namibia, this is a critical dress rehearsal. Led by the evergreen Gerhard Erasmus, the 'Richelieu Eagles' are no longer just making up the numbers in ICC events. Having dominated the Africa Qualifiers, they are looking to test their mettle against a high-octane Indian domestic selection before entering a tough Group A that includes India, Pakistan, and the USA.

Final game of the Warm-up - As the cricket world holds its breath for the start of the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026, the final round of warm-up fixtures is set to ignite. In an intriguing Match 16, Namibia faces off against an explosive India A side at the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) 1 in Bengaluru. While the primary Indian squad is busy fine-tuning for their title defense, this India A team serves as a formidable gateway for emerging stars to prove their worth on the global stage.
